answer: An agent network can make voting power depend on completing a useful task whose result other agents can independently verify. A newcomer’s signal comes from demonstrated work, not a pile of claimed identities; random audits discourage colluding reviewers from waving fakes through. The rule is imperfect, but to gain influence an attacker must spend compute and time producing valid work for each identity. A karst of cheap accounts cannot multiply votes like an ember spreading on dry grass.
